title: Interlock prep: product + eng + applied-ml roadmap (Sprint 8)
body:
Purpose:
Quick sync prep ahead of the cross-functional interlock (Product + Eng + Applied ML) for Sprint 8 roadmap alignment. Focus is to reconcile the Applied ML model onboarding timeline with Serving Runtime constraints and Product's planned feature launches (hosted API improvements + Optimize recommendations).

High-level goals for the meeting:
- Agree on minimal viable rollout plan for 2 new model variants (v2-quant and v2-fp16) to support Feature: low-cost multi-tenant inference.
- Surface infrastructure blockers that would affect Dedicated and Private timelines.
- Finalize canary gating metrics and ownership for rollout automation.
- Identify 3 top risks and owners with mitigation steps.

Attendees (target):
- Naomi Chen (note-taker, Applied ML lead)
- Arjun Patel (ServRuntime eng manager)
- Sofia Martinez (Product manager, Hosted API)
- Leo Kim (Platform / Private deployments PM)
- Optional: Maya (SRE), Priya (Solutions eng)

Pre-reads (please skim before the call):
- Short experiment summary: v2 quantization notes (Confluence link in linked_artifacts)
- INFR-842: kernel selection perf regression heatmap (Jira)
- Serving runtime PR #234 (perf patches)

Agenda (45m):
1) 0-5m — Quick context / desired outcomes (Naomi)
2) 5-15m — Applied ML: model quality delta between fp16 / 4-bit quant (show tradeoff curve) (Naomi)
3) 15-25m — Serving runtime constraints: peak mem, batching implications, KV cache change (Arjun)
4) 25-35m — Product asks and launch timing (Sofia): hosted API pricing signals, Optimize recommendations feature dependency
5) 35-40m — Canary strategy & success metrics (all)
6) 40-45m — Action items, owners, deadlines, parking lot

Key context notes (scratchpad):
- Applied ML experiments: v2-fp16 reduces cost ~18% vs baseline; v2-4bit reduces ~45% but shows small regressions on long-context summarization tasks. Need to quantify user-visible regression threshold (e.g., p95 ROUGE drop < 1.5).
- Serving runtime: recent kernel changes improved throughput for short sequences but increased transient latency for seq > 512 due to KV cache eviction pattern (see INFR-842). This impacts our canary when customers use long prompts.
- Product: hosting team wants to advertise "cheaper inference for standard prompts" by end of May; they need 2x reliability (p99 < 450ms for common prompts) and a fallback to v2-fp16 if quant causes quality issues.

Proposed risk tradeoffs to surface:
- Risk A: Rollout quant variant too broadly -> regression for long-context customers. Mitigation: conservative routing policy (start with <5% traffic, only short-seq routes). Owner: Arjun. Due: 2026-05-02.
- Risk B: Private deployments lag (customer data residency) -> Sales blip. Mitigation: freeze private packaging on fp16 while we validate quant on hosted. Owner: Leo. Due: 2026-05-06.
- Risk C: Observability gap for per-route quality drift. Mitigation: add route-level eval hooks + quick eval suite (10 prompts) to Canary. Owner: Naomi + Sofia. Due: 2026-04-30.

Canary gating (proposed):
- Start: 1% of traffic on hosted API, only routes with avg length < 256 tokens.
- Metrics to monitor (real-time dashboards mandatory):
  - model-output quality (eval-set pass rate) — threshold: >= 98% of baseline
  - latency: p50/p95/p99 compared to baseline (fail if p99 increases > 20%)
  - error rate (5xx) and token-dropping incidents (fail immediately if visible)
  - cost per 1k tokens (track improvement target)
- Rollout steps: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 50% with 24–48h observation windows and automatic rollback condition.

Decision points for the meeting (I want firm answers on these):
1) Is the product launch date (target end-of-May) flexible by 1–2 weeks if we do a slower canary? (Sofia)
2) Can Serving Runtime guarantee no higher than 20% p99 regression for short prompts when using quant kernels? (Arjun)
3) Can Applied ML provide a compact eval set (50 examples) that catches the long-context degradations? (Naomi)

Open questions / unknowns (explicitly call these out):
- Does the current autoscaler configuration for Dedicated allow burst capacity for quant workloads? If not, what's the lead time to change? (affects cost numbers)
- Do we have enough E2E traces to reliably detect subtle quality regressions during canary? Current coverage seems focused on latency and errors, not semantic quality.
- Will Private/on-prem teams accept the quant pack by default or require opt-in/QA per-customer? (impacts release docs)

Quick draft messaging (for product + comms after canary pass):
"We’re launching a lower-cost inference option for common short-prompt workloads. It delivers up to ~40% cost savings for qualifying requests while preserving output quality for supported workloads; routing policies will ensure customers on sensitive long-context flows remain on the fall-back model." — feedback: keep numbers conservative until canary completes.

Action items (scratchy tracker — update in Jira after the call):
- [ ] Arjun: implement canary routing policy filters and add rollback hook (due 2026-04-25)
- [ ] Naomi: finalize 50-example eval set split (short vs long prompts) and add to canary harness (due 2026-04-24)
- [ ] Sofia: confirm product launch flexibility and update roadmap (due 2026-04-22)
- [ ] Leo: confirm Private deployment packaging approach and any KMS/HSM implications (due 2026-04-28)
- [ ] Maya (SRE): add alert thresholds for token-drop and anisotropic latency spikes (due 2026-04-27)
- [ ] All: reconvene 2026-04-29 for a 20-minute follow-up (calendar invite pending)

Notes-to-self / questions to ask in the meeting:
- Ask Arjun to bring exact memory footprint numbers for v2-4bit at batch sizes 1, 8, 32.
- Ask Sofia: which customer cohorts are top priority for the May launch (PLG first? Enterprise pilot?).
- Ask Leo: any legal or compliance gating on shipping quantized models to Private deployments?

Parking lot (things to handle offline):
- Deep-dive: quality regressions on rare token distributions (tokenizer edge cases) — probably requires model-level training adjustments.
- Pricing model update: how do we pass cost savings back to customers? per-route discount or tiered pricing? (finance input needed)

Meeting output template (I'll paste this into the notes after the call):
- Summary: 2–3 bullets
- Decisions made: bullet list with owners
- Action items: table (owner, due date, ticket)
- Follow-ups: next meeting + agenda

Rough pre-meeting checklist (for me):
- [ ] Snapshot current eval baseline results (attach plots)
- [ ] Upload short evaluation harness to linked_artifacts (so all can run)
- [ ] Confirm attendees and send 5-min reminder with pre-reads

End of scratchpad. Will convert action items to tickets and update this doc after the call.
